subject: Dedicated capacity sizing: safety margin, slotting and telemetry alignment
messages:
From: Tyler Reed <tyler@brightpath.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — renewal coming up; usage spike and sizing ask

Jonas / Redwood team,

Renewal for BrightPath's Dedicated pool is due in mid-July. Over the last 6 weeks we've consistently seen a 65% increase in tail concurrency and several 99th-percentile latency spikes during peak ML training windows. Before we lock in commits we'd like a sizing recommendation that: 1) covers our expected Q3 burst (est. +40% vs current usage), 2) includes a clear "safety margin" for sudden marketing-driven spikes, and 3) specifies what telemetry/observability you'll provide so our SREs can validate on day-1.

Can Redwood put together a short proposal with recommended GPU add, slotting strategy, and the telemetry/events you will surface (per-token latency breakdown, batch sizes, cache hit rates)? We need this to present to procurement and engineering by July 3.

Attached: our exported usage_summary (CSV) for May–Jun.

Thanks,
Tyler
Director of Infrastructure
BrightPath AI

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Tyler Reed <tyler@brightpath.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — renewal coming up; usage spike and sizing ask

Tyler — thanks for the heads up and for the CSV. We reviewed the high-level numbers and can get you a concise plan by July 2. High level upfront: we recommend a two-stage plan — a short buffer (safety margin) to cover Q3 bursts and a staggered slotting change so you only pay for added GPU capacity when you need peak concurrency.

Next steps from our side:
- Internal sizing calc and utilization sensitivity (will attach).
- Proposal PDF with pricing and a minimal SLA addendum for the added tranche.
- Telemetry checklist we can enable on day-1 (token latencies, per-route throughput, cache-hit %, batch histograms, per-token cost signals).

Ben, Laura — tagging you for sizing and telemetry items. Can you pull the last 90 days of tail-concurrency and KV-cache hit rates and draft a recommended tranche (GPU count + quantile target)?

Tyler — I'll circulate a formal proposal and a link to the draft spreadsheet by end of day Monday. If possible, please confirm the procurement contact and preferred DocuSign flow.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sizing details and safety margin calc (internal)

Jonas / Laura — I pulled the Q2 exports and ran utilization sensitivity with three scenarios: conservative (+20%), expected (+40%), aggressive (+70%). Key findings attached (usage_report_q2.csv, initial_estimate_v1.xlsx):

- Current steady-state GPU slots: 120 slot-equivalents (mixed A100/V100 profile).
- Observed tail concurrency growth: 65% over baseline across the 99th pct windows during marketing tests.
- Average KV-cache hit rate: 72% (drops to ~55% during batch-heavy windows).

Recommendation (short form):
1) Immediate buffer tranche: +18 slot-equivalents (15% safety margin) to absorb Q3 initial surges.
2) Staged scaling policy: implement an autoslice that adds up to +36 slot-equivalents on verified SLA breach (based on 95th/99th latency thresholds) — billed as burst credits if used.
3) Observability: enable per-route batch histograms, prefix-KV hit alerts, and a token-latency heatmap for the next 90 days.

I've put the detailed math in proposed_sizing.xlsx and flagged assumptions (token lengths, batch efficiencies, quantization options). If procurement wants a firm commit instead of burst credits, the equivalent committed tranche would be +12 slots with a different per-slot rate (see sheet).

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Tyler Reed <tyler@brightpath.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: immediate buffer + staged autoslice for BrightPath renewal (BPATH-2028-EX-23)

Tyler — attaching the formal proposal (proposed_sizing_and_pricing.pdf) and the underlying sizing workbook. TL;DR: we recommend an initial committed buffer of +18 slot-equivalents (15% safety margin) to cover expected Q3 bursts, plus an autoslice that allows BrightPath to access an additional +36 slot-equivalents as burst credits when pre-defined latency thresholds are crossed.

What we will deliver on day-1 of the tranche:
- Dedicated GPU add (inventory mapped to your region).
- Observability package: token latency histogram, per-route batch size distribution, prefix/KV cache hit rate dashboards, tail-concurrency alerts and traces.
- Rollout plan: canary 24–48h, full ramp in 72h after sign-off.

Commercials: two options in the PDF — committed buffer (monthly rate, lower per-slot price) or buffer + burst credits (lower upfront but with overage for sustained burst usage). Procurement folks typically prefer the committed buffer for predictability.

Please review and confirm if procurement prefers the committed buffer or the buffer+burst model. Once confirmed, I'll send the DocuSign and route it to our finance/legal templates. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12435/BPATH-2028-EX-23

Regards,
Jonas

From: Tyler Reed <tyler@brightpath.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightpath.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: immediate buffer + staged autoslice for BrightPath renewal (BPATH-2028-EX-23)

Jonas — thanks, the proposal looks sensible. Procurement prefers predictability, but finance is wary of a large committed add. Two asks before we sign: 1) can you shrink the committed buffer to +12 slots (instead of +18) and make the autoslice allow a slightly larger burst (+42) so we have a smoother cost profile? 2) we need a day-1 telemetry runbook that our SREs can follow — sample queries/alert thresholds.

If you can send an updated PDF with those two changes we can route to legal and sign within 48 hours.

—Tyler

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Tyler Reed <tyler@brightpath.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: immediate buffer + staged autoslice for BrightPath renewal (BPATH-2028-EX-23)

Tyler — absolutely. Ben and I updated the workbook and the commercial in the attached PDF: committed buffer now +12 slots; autoslice expanded to +42 burst slots; we've re-run the cost sims and included a blended month-1 vs steady-state comparison. Also attached: a telemetry runbook (short doc in the Drive link) with sample alert thresholds (95th token latency > 220ms for high-priority paths, KV cache drop < 60% triggers pre-emptive autoslice).

I'll open the DocuSign envelope once you confirm procurement contact details and billing entity. Targeting a canary roll on July 8 if signed by July 4.

Thanks — looking forward to greenlighting the rollout.
Jonas

---
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
